clue.text: European means to be heard in argument

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
a mic (microphone) is the means by which a speaker is heard

explanation.surface: A European finds a way to make their voice heard in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a strongly worded attack or controversial case, a kind of argument.

clue.text: After bout, stop to see if characters are OK

definitions.text: to see if characters are OK

parts.note: a bout is a spell, a period of some activity
to check is to halt or stop

explanation.surface: After a round of fighting, a pause to see whether the boxers are all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people, but it means the letters of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a spelling checker is verifying that the letters typed in a document are correct.

clue.text: This makes MP a deputy leader

parts.note: in the NATO alphabet ... stands for M, and P is the abbreviation for ..., so the two names together spell out M and P

explanation.surface: A recipe for promoting a Member of Parliament to deputy leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue's MP is what it produces. Mike Pence was Donald Trump's vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: A US vice-president is second in command to the president, a deputy leader of the nation.

clue.text: Worst family turns up for Allen Ginsberg?

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat or beat them

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word for family is read from bottom to top

parts.note: kin means one's family

explanation.surface: A poet's worst relatives make an appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Ginsberg as an example of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg was a leading poet of the 1950s Beat Generation, a typical example of the movement.

clue.text: Oily stuff: it's about to keep hairdo wonderful

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the turned letters wrap round the rest
about here means turned round, so the letters of it's run backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters, without the apostrophe
a perm is a hairstyle with set curls
ace is slang for excellent or wonderful

explanation.surface: A hair product that is oily is said to keep a hairstyle looking great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IT'S to STI, and 'to keep' wraps it round PERM and ACE. Spermaceti comes from the sperm whale, not from anything a hairdresser uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Spermaceti is the waxy oil found in the head of the sperm whale, once used for candles and ointments.

clue.text: Go crazy the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the slang word for mad is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Go mad by heading off in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun: have a go, have a try.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is an attempt or try, as in having a stab at something.

clue.text: French playmaker again protects position of ball

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the word for again goes round the other piece

parts.note: more can mean again, as in 'once more'
in golf the lie is the position in which the ball comes to rest

explanation.surface: A French football playmaker again shields the ball's position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playmaker' suggests football but here means a maker of plays, a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic dramatist, a writer of plays.

clue.text: Change popular stimulant for analgesic

parts.note: to morph is to transform or change
in means fashionable or popular
E is short for ecstasy, a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: Swapping a popular stimulant for a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphine is a strong opiate drug used to relieve pain, which is what an analgesic does.

clue.text: Idle, maybe cold-blooded creature

definitions.meaning: Eric Idle was a member of the Monty ... comedy team
a large constricting snake, a reptile

explanation.surface: A lazy, perhaps heartless, being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' poses as lazy but is Eric Idle, of the British comedy troupe Monty Python.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle was one of the Monty Python team; separately a constricting snake, a cold-blooded reptile.

clue.text: Determined chap's going to peak close to Everest

parts.note: he'll, short for he will, says a man is going to do something
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A determined man means to reach a summit near Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' is the Scottish word for a mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent describes someone utterly resolved on something, whatever the consequences.

clue.text: Poor sportsman in boozer's back part

indicators.note: back means the word for pub is read the other way

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub or bar
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A weak player hangs around the back part of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabbit is a weak, unskilled player, especially a poor batsman in cricket or a novice in golf or tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In British sporting slang a hopeless player, such as a tailend cricket batter, is called this.

clue.text: Is it grave or serious? In dark, I am confused

indicators.note: the word for serious sits in the middle of the jumbled letters
confused means the letters of dark, I and am are muddled up

parts.note: a critical situation is a serious one

explanation.surface: Someone in the dark asks whether a situation is grave or serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles the letters of DARK, I and AM, and 'In' places CRITICAL among them. 'grave' poses as solemn but is the grave accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave accent is one of the signs written above letters to change pronunciation, alongside the acute and cedilla.

clue.text: Rambling in rocky north-east? Nice!

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east
taken as written, the French city

explanation.surface: Out walking in the rugged north-east and enjoying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' looks like a hike but means talking disjointedly. 'rocky' shuffles NORTH, E and NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that wanders without clear connection is incoherent, lacking logical order.

clue.text: Sort of pig in soy with MSG in it getting cooked

indicators.note: cooking a dish mixes it up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pork in soy sauce with monosodium glutamate, being cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cooked' shuffles IN SOY, MSG and IT. A male chauvinist is called a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogynist is a woman-hater, the sort of man scornfully labelled a male chauvinist pig.

clue.text: See 3
Anxious for the future, say

definitions.meaning: the future is one of the verb forms in grammar, along with the past and present

explanation.surface: Worried about what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means nervous and strained; also a grammatical time form of verbs, of which the future is one.

clue.text: Privates are behind this English flag, if ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand to attention behind an English flag when commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privates' look like soldiers on parade, but they are private parts.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical art a fig leaf covers the genitals of nude figures, so they are hidden behind it.

clue.text: Faithless sort cheers up on the job

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece is on top of the next, so the word for thanks comes before the robbery
in a down entry, up means the word for thanks is read bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a job is criminal slang for a robbery, a heist

explanation.surface: An unbeliever is cheered up by the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ta' is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has no belief in any god is without religious faith.

clue.text: It turns in either direction

definitions.note: something that turns or spins round is described by these words, and the word for it reads the same both ways

indicators.note: the letters read the same whichever way they are taken, forwards or back

parts.note: something that turns or spins round is described by these words, and the word for it reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Something that spins both clockwise and anticlockwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in either direction' seems to describe the spinning but says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates or spins round, such as a muscle or a machine part.

clue.text: London dignitary, proverbially clever fellow with striking fashion

parts.note: a smart-alec is called a clever dick in a common saying
hitting means striking
the ton is an old word for high fashion or society

explanation.surface: A smart London official with a forceful style.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Whittington was Lord Mayor of London, famous from pantomime and his cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Whittington was several times Lord Mayor of London, the city's ceremonial chief.

clue.text: After Salah's header, Aussie player is to dribble

indicators.note: the tennis player comes after the first letter of the footballer
the header of a word is its first letter, with a nod to football

parts.note: Rod Laver is a great Australian tennis player

explanation.surface: After a header from footballer Mohamed Salah, an Australian is about to dribble the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dribble' looks like football but means drool.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, to drool.

clue.text: One in vehicle looking in the mirror a lot?

definitions.text: looking in the mirror a lot?

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A driver in a van checks the mirror often.
explanation.walkthrough: The mirror looks like a driving mirror, but it is a vain person admiring themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person constantly admires their own reflection, preening and full of self-regard.

clue.text: College member acquiring second language

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so S goes inside the word for the pupil

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil of Eton College

explanation.surface: A schoolboy picks up a second language.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonian is the Finnic tongue spoken in Estonia, a Baltic country.

clue.text: What could be an improvement in the weather

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the clue's first word might become a different word

explanation.surface: A question about what might make the weather better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be' reads as a question opener, but it shuffles WHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw is the melting of ice and snow as the temperature rises, a welcome turn for the better.

clue.text: Helping one to enter shop

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the phrase for informing

parts.note: to shop someone is to inform on them, to rat on them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Assisting someone to get into a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is British slang for informing on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed portion of food, a helping or allocation.

clue.text: Busts attractive in photo

parts.note: snaps means breaks or busts
hot is slang for sexy or attractive

explanation.surface: A racy picture shows a bust looking attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busts' looks like a noun for chests, but it is a verb meaning breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly.
